reviewed_by: Delegated coding agent source-semantic review against the live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 MCP view and Radare2 6.2.0 on retail igi.exe (SHA-256 dea34892...); the candidate translation unit was recompiled with the repository -O3 -DNDEBUG flags and its object symbol compared with the body recorded for the previous source digest.
source_revision: worktree HEAD 5a3b6e40521b2159f6dce7e8ecbeafb8fe3b9b91 plus the uncommitted Qvm_ReportError correction; bound by engine/src/retail/script/qvm_native_loader.cpp sha256 48ae1e2700dfc8738d9ea1a31178495ff821c3bed69ac189263a88eebac8359f
review_basis: The current engine/src/retail/script/qvm_native_loader.cpp hashes to 48ae1e2700dfc8738d9ea1a31178495ff821c3bed69ac189263a88eebac8359f. The retail entry was re-read through the live Binary Ninja view and independently recovered with Radare2 on 2026-10-23; both live graphs are identical to the bound artifacts, so the recorded CFG is current. The candidate was recompiled from that source; its object symbol body was compared with the body compiled from the previous source digest 655494c9... and is instruction-identical after relocation resolution, proving the Qvm_ReportError edit did not alter this function. This review supersedes the earlier evidence that was stale against the current source digest.

retail_function.name: Qvm_Cleanup
retail_function.summary: 0x004B83D0-0x004B8405 (55 bytes), 3 basic blocks / 2 edges, cdecl int32_t(void* qvm): loads the dword at qvm+0x8C; when non-zero calls 0x004BD380(standalone) (recorded by Binary Ninja as Sys_CheckHeap_28 and ported as the standalone-release boundary), otherwise calls Resource_Unload(qvm) (0x004B6380); both paths then call 0x004B0D10(qvm) (Mem_DeAllocFn, the block-release boundary) and return its EAX. No writes to qvm.

checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: Binary Ninja and Radare2 both recover 0x004B83D0-0x004B8405 with 3 blocks / 2 edges; the live re-read matches the bound artifacts exactly (similarity 1.000). The candidate symbol igi::retail::script::Qvm_Cleanup(void*) is the body implementing that entry, 80 bytes including alignment padding.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.rationale: Retail reads the single stack argument at [esp+8] into ESI and forwards it unchanged to each release callee; the candidate declares void* qvm and forwards it unchanged. cdecl and the 32-bit int return are preserved.

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.rationale: The only constant is the object field offset 0x8C; the candidate reads the same offset (bytes+0x8C). No arithmetic or scaling.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.rationale: The branch test on qvm+0x8C and the call order (standalone release and then block release, or Resource_Unload and then block release) match retail, with the same single pointer argument. The two release callees 0x004BD380 and 0x004B0D10 are not transcribed and are invoked through injectable g_sys_qvm_standalone_release / g_sys_qvm_block_release boundaries whose null default skips the call and returns 0; that substitution is a recorded limitation, not behavioural equivalence.

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.rationale: Pointer/dword handling and calls only; no floating-point data or instructions.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.rationale: Retail reads a 32-bit dword at qvm+0x8C and writes nothing to the object; the candidate reads a std::uint32_t at bytes+0x8C with the same width and performs no store to qvm.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: Both retail paths converge on the block-release call and return its EAX (EAX survives pop esi); the candidate returns the block-release boundary result on both paths, so the return sites match even though the default boundary yields 0.

signature_comparison.rationale: Binary Ninja reports int32_t(int32_t* arg1) and Radare2 recovers cdecl with one stack argument; the candidate declares std::int32_t Qvm_Cleanup(void*). Pointer typing is ABI-identical and the int32_t return is preserved.

limitations: No paired retail/candidate game-process runtime capture exists for this address; runtime_tests and behavioral are intentionally absent and RUNTIME_TESTED/VERIFIED are not claimed.
The CFG agreement cited here is Binary Ninja vs Radare2 on the retail image; cfg_similarity 1.0 is not a candidate-vs-retail CFG score, and the candidate machine CFG was not compared for isomorphism.
The candidate object was rebuilt and hashed, but the image was not linked by this review; no linked-image or receipt claim is made.

The release callees 0x004BD380 (standalone) and 0x004B0D10 (block) remain unported. With the default null boundaries the candidate skips both releases and returns 0 where retail returns the 0x004B0D10 result; the object is therefore not freed until the integration installs the boundaries.

The compiled object body is byte-for-byte identical to the 80-byte body recorded for source 655494c9... (symbol offset 0x1A0 in the previous object, 0x1B0 in the current object because Qvm_ReportError grew by 16 bytes), so the Qvm_ReportError edit provably did not change this function.

The binary_ninja and radare2 evidence signatures bound here were re-derived from the current artifacts (int32_t(int32_t* arg1) and fcn.004b83d0 (int32_t arg_8h);); the manifest previously said 'not restated'.
